entries.title: MySQL / MariaDB binary log
entries.what: The database's change log: every write is recorded here, used for replication and point-in-time recovery. Files are numbered (binlog.000001, mysql-bin.000002, …) and MySQL keeps an index of them.
entries.safetyText: Don't delete them by hand while MySQL is running: the index still lists them and replication or backups may need them. Let MySQL purge old ones.
entries.whyBig: Each file grows up to 1 GB (max_binlog_size) and the default keeps 30 days, so busy development databases collect dozens of gigabytes.
howTo: Connect to MySQL as an admin.
Purge logs older than a few days (or up to a given file).
To keep it small automatically, set an expiry time.

commands.label: Purge logs older than 3 days
commands.text: PURGE BINARY LOGS BEFORE NOW() - INTERVAL 3 DAY;

commands.label: Keep only 3 days from now on
Using Docker
commands.text: docker exec -it <container> mysql -uroot -p -e "PURGE BINARY LOGS BEFORE NOW() - INTERVAL 3 DAY;"

entries.search: mysql binlog PURGE BINARY LOGS free space

entries.title: MySQL / InnoDB data files
entries.what: The actual database: tables, indexes and the transaction log (ibdata1, ib_logfile*, #innodb_redo, *.ibd).
entries.safetyText: Deleting these destroys or corrupts the database. Drop tables or databases from MySQL instead.
howTo: Find big tables with SQL, then drop or truncate what you don't need.
To shrink ibdata1 itself, dump and re-import the databases.

commands.label: Largest tables
commands.text: SELECT table_schema, table_name, ROUND((data_length+index_length)/1024/1024) AS mb FROM information_schema.tables ORDER BY mb DESC LIMIT 20;

entries.title: PostgreSQL write-ahead log (pg_wal)
entries.what: PostgreSQL's transaction log, needed to recover after a crash.
entries.safetyText: Deleting WAL files by hand corrupts the database. If it keeps growing, a replication slot or archiving is usually stuck.
howTo: Check for unused replication slots and drop them.
Let PostgreSQL recycle WAL with a checkpoint.

entries.title: Redis snapshot (dump.rdb / appendonly.aof)
entries.what: Redis's saved copy of its data, loaded on restart.
entries.safetyText: Deleting it loses Redis's stored data at the next restart.

entries.title: Database logs
entries.what: Error, slow-query or general logs of MySQL, PostgreSQL or MongoDB.
entries.safetyText: Old logs are safe to remove; the database keeps writing a new one. The general log can grow very fast: turn it off if you don't need it.
